related_questions.question: Why are people suddenly getting COVID-19 again?
related_questions.snippet: Once you have had COVID-19, your immune system responds in several ways. This immune response can protect you against reinfection for several months, but this protection decreases over time. People with weakened immune systems who get an infection may have a limited immune response or none at all.

related_questions.question: How likely am I to get COVID if I am fully vaccinated?
related_questions.snippet: While the three COVID-19 vaccines we have are incredibly effective, no vaccine provides 100% protection against the virus. People who are fully or partially vaccinated can still become infected by the novel coronavirus, which is called a breakthrough infection.

text_blocks.snippet: COVID-19 breakthrough infections refer to instances where a fully vaccinated individual contracts the virus. While vaccines are highly effective, they don't offer complete protection, and breakthrough infections can still occur. These infections are generally less severe than those in unvaccinated individuals, with fewer hospitalizations and deaths.
snippet_highlighted_words: refer to instances where a fully vaccinated individual contracts the virus

list.title: Vaccines are not 100% effective:
list.snippet: Breakthrough infections highlight that vaccines, while significantly reducing the risk of infection, illness, and severe outcomes, don't eliminate the possibility of contracting COVID-19.

list.title: Severity is typically lower:
list.snippet: Studies have shown that breakthrough infections tend to be less severe, with fewer hospitalizations and deaths compared to unvaccinated individuals.

list.title: Variant-specific considerations:
list.snippet: The effectiveness of vaccines can vary depending on the circulating variants of the virus and the specific vaccine used. Medical sources say there may be some cross-reactivity between vaccine variants and variants of concern, but this is an area of ongoing research.

list.title: Importance of continued precautions:
list.snippet: Even with vaccination, it's crucial to continue practicing preventative measures like mask-wearing in public indoor settings, social distancing, and good hygiene to minimize the risk of transmission and breakthrough infections.

list.title: Focus on public health:
list.snippet: Understanding breakthrough infections is important for public health efforts, including vaccine development, booster strategies, and ongoing monitoring of the virus's behavior.
